 Medium

 Print EPFO New Delhi: Employees' Provident Fund Organisation is set to unveil a systematic withdrawal plan meant to allow voluntary contributions by gig and unorganised sector workers, while also giving crores of its existing subscribers the option to use the instrument since many are unable to invest their retirement corpus prudently. The proposal is scheduled to be discussed by the central board of trustees headed by labour minister Mansukh Mandaviya on Thursday. To begin with, the voluntary scheme is meant to focus on existing subscribers, with EPFO estimating that 6.3 lakh members who are above 55 years at present could be potential beneficiaries in the initial phase. Long-term savings Currently, they have to withdraw the entire corpus within three years of retirement, before their account turns inoperative, meaning it will stop earning annual interest. Instead, they will now be given the option to withdraw a part of the funds, which can be done periodically - monthly, quarterly or annually. The withdrawal period can extend up to a prescribed tenure and the funds will remain invested in EPF and continue to earn interest, people familiar with the proposal told TOI. Subscribers will also have the option to stop the SWP whenever they want to, apart from partial lump-sum withdrawal or only withdrawing the interest earned. EPFO to allow micro-contributions like tips
 EPFO may soon give members the option to make voluntary contributions into their EPF account through digital means, with the employer not required to make any matching contribution. The contributions will, however, be in line with limits prescribed under Income Tax Act. The system is proposed to be opened up for gig and unorganised sector workers. EPFO will also allow micro-contributions, such as tips, gratuity and gifts through a universal account number-linked digital payment mechanism. The labour ministry has been looking to use EPF as a tool for long-term savings by gig and unorganised sector workers since the new Social Security Code was implemented, but Centre has to extend SWP to the sector so domestic workers, construction workers, street vendors and others are included under the umbrella.  Those familiar with the with tax benefits available on investments and interest income up to Rs 2.5 lakh annually. Calculations by EPFO indicate those opting for SWPs will earn more than what bank fixed deposits or annuities fetch. The move will not create any liability on EPFO or govt but allow for better management of funds by individuals. Once approved by the central board of trustees, EPFO will have to put in place technology to deal with additional work. The proposal will not be applicable at present to exempted establishments, which self-manage their provident funds in accord with EPFO norms.
